intervals.label: observations
intervals.note: The 2010 BICEP paper says "During three seasons of observing at the South Pole (2006 through 2008)"; the end is recorded at year precision (the last observing month is not stated).
intervals.quote: BICEP has completed 3 years of successful observations at the South Pole beginning in 2006 February.

intervals.label: observations ended
intervals.note: No source states a decommissioning date; BICEP1 "observed ... between 2006 and 2008" (LAMBDA), "three seasons of observations at the South Pole (2006 to 2008)" (arXiv:1310.1422), so completion is recorded at year precision, 2008.
intervals.quote: During three seasons of observing at the South Pole (2006 through 2008)

placements.note: Start is the first month of observations; the telescope was in the DSL building 800 m from the pole.
placements.quote: looking out through the roof of the Dark Sector Laboratory (DSL) building located 800 m from the geographic South Pole

summary.plain: A small two-lens refracting telescope looking out through the roof of a laboratory near the South Pole, built to look for the faint polarization pattern that gravitational waves from inflation would leave in the Big Bang afterglow.
summary.technical: Two-lens refracting telescope with 49 pairs of horn-coupled polarization-sensitive bolometers at 100 and 150 GHz, on a 3-axis mount in the Dark Sector Laboratory; observed 2006-2008, mapping about 2% of the sky.

technology.quote: The instrument comprised a two-lens refracting telescope coupled to a focal plane of 49 orthogonal pairs of horn-coupled polarization-sensitive bolometers operating at 100 and 150 GHz.
technology.value: Two-lens refracting telescope with a focal plane of 49 orthogonal pairs of horn-coupled polarization-sensitive bolometers at 100 and 150 GHz.
